title: Master Services Agreement: Fees, Invoicing and Payment Schedule
sections: This schedule forms part of the Master Services Agreement between Halvorsen Digital Ltd (the Supplier) and {client} (the Customer) and sets out how fees are invoiced and paid. It applies to all statements of work signed under the agreement unless a statement of work expressly overrides a clause by number. Fees are quoted and invoiced in {currency}, and exchange rate risk sits with the Supplier. The Customer's accounts payable contact for all invoicing matters is {person} ({email}). The Supplier's commercial contact is {person_2}, who must be copied on any notice that concerns overdue amounts, credit notes or suspension of services. Where this schedule conflicts with the main agreement, this schedule prevails for payment matters only.

The Supplier invoices monthly in arrears on the first working day of each month for time and materials work, and on milestone acceptance for fixed price work. Every invoice must quote the Customer purchase order number, the statement of work reference and the billing period. Invoices are submitted through {invoice_portal}; invoices sent by email only are not deemed received. An invoice that is missing a purchase order number may be rejected within five working days, and the payment clock restarts when a corrected invoice is submitted. Expenses are rebilled at cost with receipts, capped at ten percent of the fees in the same invoice unless approved in advance and in writing by the Customer's project sponsor.

Undisputed invoices are payable within {payment_days} days of the date of receipt. Payment is made by bank transfer to the Supplier account stated here, {iban}, and the Supplier will never change its bank details by email alone: any change is confirmed by a signed letter and a call back to a number already on file. Remittance advice should be sent to the Supplier's finance team on the day payment is released. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, payment is due on the next working day. Early payment discounts are not offered under this agreement, and no set-off is permitted against fees except for service credits that both parties have agreed in writing.

If the Customer wishes to dispute an invoice, it must notify the Supplier in writing within {dispute_window} of receipt, stating the disputed amount and the reason. The undisputed portion must still be paid on time. The finance leads of both parties will meet within ten working days to resolve the dispute, escalating to the executive sponsors if it remains open after thirty days. Amounts that are overdue and not disputed accrue interest at {late_interest}, calculated daily from the due date until payment in full. If an undisputed invoice remains unpaid thirty days after a written reminder, the Supplier may suspend non-critical services on fourteen days' notice, but may not withhold data or access to deliverables already paid for.

Rates are fixed for the first twelve months from the effective date. After that, the Supplier may increase rates once per contract year by giving ninety days' written notice, and any increase is capped at {fee_increase_cap}. Rate increases never apply to fixed price statements of work already signed. The Customer may request an annual rate benchmark at its own cost, and both parties will negotiate in good faith if the benchmark shows rates more than fifteen percent above the market median. This schedule is governed by {governing_law}, and any payment claim below the small claims threshold may be brought in that forum without first using the escalation process in the main agreement.

title: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement
sections: This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement is made between Halvorsen Digital Ltd and {counterparty}, each of which may disclose and receive confidential information. The information is shared solely for the purpose of {purpose}, and the receiving party may not use it for any other purpose, including benchmarking, product development or reverse engineering. Each party appoints a single point of contact for the exchange: for Halvorsen this is {person} ({email}). No licence to any patent, trade mark or copyright is granted by disclosure, and nothing in this agreement obliges either party to proceed with any transaction. Each party bears its own costs in connection with the evaluation, including the fees of its own advisers.

Confidential information means any information disclosed in writing, orally or by demonstration that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including source code, pricing, customer lists, roadmaps and personal data. Information disclosed orally or visually is protected only if the disclosing party confirms its confidential nature in a written summary within {marking_days} of disclosure. Information is not confidential if it is or becomes public through no fault of the recipient, was already lawfully known to the recipient, is independently developed without use of the information, or is received from a third party free of any duty of confidence. The burden of proving that an exclusion applies rests on the recipient.

The recipient will protect confidential information with at least the care it uses for its own information of similar sensitivity, and never less than reasonable care. Access is limited to employees, officers, professional advisers and approved subcontractors who need to know it for the purpose and who are bound by written duties at least as strict as these. The recipient is responsible for any breach by those people. If the recipient is required by law, a regulator or a court order to disclose information, it will give prompt notice where lawful, disclose only the minimum required and cooperate with any attempt to obtain a protective order. Copies may only be made where strictly necessary for the purpose.

This agreement covers disclosures made during a period of {term_years} from the effective date. The obligations of confidence continue for {survival_years} after the end of that period, except that obligations relating to trade secrets and source code continue for as long as the information remains a trade secret. On written request, or at the end of the disclosure period, the recipient will return or securely destroy all confidential information within {return_days} and confirm destruction in writing signed by an officer. Copies held in routine backup systems may be retained until overwritten in the normal cycle, provided they are not accessed and remain subject to this agreement.

Each party acknowledges that damages alone may not be an adequate remedy for breach, and the disclosing party may seek injunctive relief without proving actual loss or posting a bond, to the extent the court allows. This agreement is governed by {governing_law}. Neither party may assign it without the other's written consent, except to a successor of its entire business. Notices must be sent to the legal department of the receiving party, with a copy by email; for the counterparty, notices go to {person_2} ({email_2}). This agreement is the entire understanding on its subject and may only be amended in writing signed by both parties.

title: Enterprise Software Licence Agreement
sections: {licensor} grants Halvorsen Digital Ltd a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to install and use {product} for its internal business operations. The licence is measured by {licence_metric} and the initial entitlement is {licence_quantity}. Use is permitted in {territory}; deployment outside that territory, including on cloud regions hosted elsewhere, needs prior written approval from the licensor. Affiliates may use the software under this licence provided Halvorsen remains responsible for their compliance. The software may not be sublicensed, rented, offered as a service to third parties or used to build a competing product. Our internal software asset owner for this licence is {person} ({email}), who keeps the entitlement register.

Halvorsen may make a reasonable number of copies for backup, disaster recovery and non-production testing, provided that standby and test environments do not process live transactions. Disaster recovery instances may be activated for up to thirty days per year without additional fees. Decompiling or reverse engineering the software is prohibited except to the extent applicable law expressly permits it for interoperability. All proprietary notices must be kept on every copy. Open source components shipped with the software are governed by their own licences, which the licensor lists in the release notes, and the licensor warrants that no component requires Halvorsen to disclose its own source code or licence its own software to others.

The licensor may verify compliance no more than once in any twelve month period, by giving at least {audit_notice} written notice. Audits take place during normal business hours, are performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and must not unreasonably disrupt operations. Halvorsen may instead provide a self-certified usage report generated by the licensor's own measurement tool. If an audit shows use above the entitlement, Halvorsen will purchase the additional licences at {overuse_rate}, and no other penalty applies. The licensor bears the audit costs unless underlicensing exceeds five percent of the entitlement, in which case Halvorsen reimburses the reasonable cost of the audit.

Annual support and maintenance is included in the first year and renews each year at the rate in the order form. Support covers bug fixes, security patches and all new minor and major versions released during the support term. The licensor's support desk is staffed {support_hours}, and severity one incidents must be acknowledged within one hour and worked continuously until a workaround is in place. Each major version is supported for at least thirty-six months after the release of its successor. If support lapses, reinstatement requires payment of the missed support fees plus a reinstatement charge of ten percent of those fees.

The licensor warrants that for ninety days after delivery the software will perform materially in line with its documentation, and that it contains no malicious code. Halvorsen's sole remedy for breach of the performance warranty is repair, replacement or a refund of the licence fee for the affected software. The licence is perpetual once the fees are paid, but the licensor may terminate it if Halvorsen commits a material breach that remains uncured thirty days after notice. On termination Halvorsen will uninstall the software and certify deletion. Commercial questions go to the licensor's account manager, {person_2}, and legal notices to the address stated in the order form.

title: Office Lease: Key Commercial Terms
sections: This summary records the key commercial terms of the lease of office premises at {building}, {city}, taken by Halvorsen Digital as tenant. The demised premises comprise {floor_area} of open plan office space together with shared use of the reception, meeting suites and bicycle store. The landlord's managing agent for day to day matters is {person} ({email}, {phone}). The lease term is ten years from the date of completion. This summary is for internal reference only: where it differs from the signed lease, the lease prevails, and any proposed change to the premises must be cleared with the workplace team before anyone contacts the landlord or the managing agent.

The annual rent is {annual_rent}, exclusive of VAT, payable quarterly in advance. A rent free period of six months applied from completion and has now expired. Rent is reviewed {rent_review}, and a review can never result in a decrease. The tenant has provided security equal to {deposit}, held in a separate designated account or instrument, and returned within two months of the end of the lease less any sums properly due. Rent paid more than fourteen days late bears interest at four percent above the base rate. Rent invoices are checked by the workplace team before payment, and any query is raised with the managing agent within ten working days.

In addition to rent, the tenant pays a service charge covering cleaning of common parts, security, lift maintenance, building insurance and the managing agent's fee. The budgeted service charge for the current year is {service_charge}, and the landlord provides a reconciled statement within six months of each year end. The tenant may inspect the invoices supporting the statement on reasonable notice. Capital improvements to the building are not recoverable through the service charge, and any single item of non-routine expenditure above twenty thousand in the local currency must be notified in advance with at least two quotes. Disputes about the service charge are referred to an independent surveyor.

The premises may be used as offices within the relevant planning class and for ancillary training and events of up to one hundred people. The building is open to occupiers {access_hours}; access outside those hours requires a booking with security at least one working day ahead and may carry an air conditioning surcharge. The tenant may install its own access control on the demised floors, provided the fire alarm remains integrated with the building system. Signage is permitted in the reception directory and on the floor lobby only. Sharing occupation with group companies is allowed without consent, but subletting part of the premises requires the landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

The tenant may terminate the lease on {break_date} by giving at least nine months' written notice, provided that the rent has been paid in full and the tenant gives vacant possession. No penalty is payable on exercise of the break. At the end of the term, or on an earlier break, the tenant must remove its fit out and reinstate the premises to the condition recorded in the schedule of condition annexed to the lease, fair wear and tear excepted. A cash settlement in lieu of reinstatement may be negotiated. Break notices must be signed by a director and approved in advance by the property committee, chaired by {person_2}.

title: Supplier Onboarding and Bank Detail Verification Procedure
sections: This procedure applies to every new supplier set up in the vendor master of {entity}, and to any change in an existing supplier's bank details. Its purpose is to stop payment fraud, in particular requests to change bank details that come from compromised or spoofed supplier email accounts. Supplier set up is owned by the vendor master team, which is kept separate from the teams that raise purchase orders and release payments. No supplier may be paid before onboarding is complete. Questions about this procedure go to the vendor master lead, {person} ({email}). A supplier whose onboarding is still incomplete after sixty days is closed and must restart the process.

The requesting budget holder submits a new supplier request with a business justification and an estimated annual spend. The supplier must then provide {kyc_documents}, together with a completed bank details form on its own letterhead signed by a director. Suppliers with an estimated annual spend above {approval_threshold} also require approval from the procurement category manager and a financial health check from a credit reference agency. Suppliers who will access our systems or personal data are routed to the information security questionnaire before any contract is signed. Sole traders and freelancers are onboarded only through the contingent labour process, not through this procedure, because of employment status checks.

Bank details are never accepted from an email alone. The vendor master team verifies every new or changed bank account by {callback_rule}. The call is made by someone other than the person who received the request, and the result is recorded in the supplier file with the date, the number called and the name of the supplier contact. A complete verification note reads, for example: account {iban} confirmed by telephone on {phone}. Where the supplier cannot be reached, the change is put on hold and the existing bank details remain in use. Any pressure to skip verification, including urgent requests from senior managers, is escalated to the fraud response team the same day.

Before activation every supplier is screened against sanctions and adverse media lists using {sanctions_tool}, and the screen is repeated automatically each night for the whole vendor master. Suppliers providing services on our premises must hold public liability insurance of at least {insurance_minimum} and provide a certificate before the first visit. Professional indemnity cover is required for consultancies and its amount is set in the contract. A positive sanctions match blocks the supplier immediately, and the compliance officer decides within two working days whether it is a false positive. The vendor master team never overrides a sanctions block on its own authority, whatever the business urgency.

The first payment to a new supplier, and the first payment after any change of bank details, is held for {first_payment_hold} and released only after a second member of the treasury team confirms the verification record. Payment runs flag any invoice paid to an account changed in the previous ninety days. Supplier records are reviewed {review_cycle}, and suppliers with no transactions in eighteen months are deactivated. Internal audit samples twenty supplier changes each quarter, and any change made without a complete verification record is reported to the audit committee as a control failure, with the name of the approver and the corrective action taken.

title: Data Processing Agreement
sections: This Data Processing Agreement applies where {processor} (the Processor) processes personal data on behalf of Halvorsen Digital (the Controller) in providing {service}. The personal data concerned covers {data_categories}. The Processor acts only on the Controller's documented instructions, which are the main agreement, this agreement and any written instruction from the Controller's data protection officer, {person} ({email}). If the Processor believes an instruction breaches data protection law, it must say so immediately and may suspend that processing until the instruction is confirmed or changed. The Processor may not process the data for its own purposes, including product analytics, benchmarking or the training of statistical models.

Personal data is stored and processed in {data_location}. Remote access from other countries is permitted only for support staff listed in the sub-processor register and only under {transfer_mechanism}. The Processor will complete a transfer impact assessment before any new transfer outside the European Economic Area and share a summary with the Controller on request. Any request by a public authority for access to the data must be challenged where there are reasonable grounds, notified to the Controller unless legally prohibited, and answered with the minimum data required. The Processor publishes a transparency report on such requests every year and tells the Controller when a new report is available.

The Controller gives general authorisation for the sub-processors listed in the annex. The Processor will give at least {subprocessor_notice} notice before adding or replacing a sub-processor, by email to the privacy mailbox and by updating its online register. The Controller may object on reasonable data protection grounds within that period; if the parties cannot agree, the Controller may terminate the affected service without penalty and receive a pro rata refund of prepaid fees. The Processor imposes the same data protection obligations on each sub-processor by written contract and remains fully liable for their performance. Emergency replacements needed to keep the service running may be notified afterwards, within five working days.

The Processor maintains the technical and organisational measures in the security annex, including encryption of personal data at rest and in transit, multi-factor authentication for all administrative access, and logging of access to production systems kept for at least twelve months. Staff with access are bound by confidentiality and trained every year. The Processor will notify the Controller of a personal data breach without undue delay and in any case within {breach_notice} of becoming aware of it, giving the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects, the likely consequences and the measures taken. Breach notifications go to the security operations line on {phone} and are then confirmed in writing.

The Processor makes available all information needed to demonstrate compliance and allows {audit_rights}. Current third party certifications and penetration test summaries are provided on request without charge. At the end of the service the Processor will, at the Controller's choice, return all personal data in a commonly used machine readable format or delete it, and will delete remaining copies, including backups, within {deletion_period}. The Processor confirms deletion in writing. The Processor assists the Controller with data subject requests, impact assessments and consultations with supervisory authorities, and may charge for that assistance only where the effort exceeds two working days in a contract year.

title: Service Level Agreement and Service Credits
sections: This Service Level Agreement forms part of the subscription agreement between {provider} and Halvorsen Digital for {service}. It defines how availability is measured, how quickly incidents are handled and what compensation applies when targets are missed. Availability is measured each calendar month at the provider's network edge, using synthetic checks run every minute from at least three regions. A minute counts as unavailable when more than five percent of checks fail or core transactions return errors. Halvorsen's service owner for this agreement is {person} ({email}), who receives the monthly service report, chairs the quarterly service review and approves any credit settlement with the provider.

The provider commits to monthly availability of {uptime_target}. Planned maintenance is excluded from the calculation only when it takes place within {maintenance_window} and is announced at least five working days ahead on the status page. Emergency maintenance to fix a critical security vulnerability is also excluded, but for no more than four hours per month. Downtime caused by Halvorsen's own systems, by force majeure events or by suspension for non-payment is excluded as well. Any other downtime, including downtime caused by the provider's hosting partners or sub-processors, counts against the target, and the provider may not reclassify an incident as maintenance after the event.

Incidents are classified by Halvorsen when reported. Priority one means the service is down or a core function is unusable for all users; priority two means a major function is degraded or unavailable for a subset of users; priority three covers minor defects and questions. The provider must respond to a priority one incident within {p1_response} and to a priority two incident within {p2_response}. A response means an engineer has acknowledged the ticket and begun work, not an automated reply. Priority one incidents get an update every thirty minutes and a written root cause analysis within five working days. The provider's duty escalation manager can be reached on {phone}.

If availability in a month falls below the target, Halvorsen is entitled to service credits calculated as a percentage of the monthly fee for the affected service, as follows: {credit_table}. Credits for missed response times are an additional two percent of the monthly fee per missed priority one response. Total credits in any month are capped at {credit_cap} of the monthly fee. Credits are applied to the next invoice and are not paid in cash, except in the final month of the agreement, when they are refunded within thirty days. Credits are a price adjustment reflecting the reduced value of the service, not an estimate of loss.

To claim a credit, Halvorsen must submit a request through the support portal within {claim_window} after the end of the affected month, referencing the incident numbers concerned. The provider will confirm or dispute the claim within ten working days using its monitoring data, which Halvorsen may verify against its own records. If availability falls below the target in three consecutive months, or in any four months out of twelve, Halvorsen may terminate the affected service on thirty days' notice without paying any early termination charge. Credits are Halvorsen's sole financial remedy for missed service levels, but they do not limit the right to terminate for chronic failure.

title: Consulting Statement of Work
sections: This Statement of Work is issued under the Master Consulting Agreement between Halvorsen Digital and {consultancy}, and describes the services for {project}. Terms not defined here have the meaning given in the master agreement. The work starts on {start_date} and is planned to run for {duration}, including a two week discovery phase whose findings may adjust the later scope by change request. The engagement is managed on the Halvorsen side by {person} ({email}), who approves timesheets, accepts deliverables and is the only person who can authorise scope changes. The consultancy's engagement lead is {person_2}, who attends the weekly steering meeting and owns the risk log.

The consultancy will provide {team}. Named key personnel may not be replaced during the engagement without Halvorsen's written consent, except for illness, parental leave or departure from the consultancy, in which case a replacement of equal seniority is proposed within ten working days and onboarded at the consultancy's cost for the first five days. Consultants work on Halvorsen premises at least two days a week and follow Halvorsen's information security and site rules. Halvorsen provides laptops and system access, and consultancy devices may not connect to the internal network. Subcontracting any part of the work requires prior written approval from the Halvorsen engagement manager.

Services are charged on a time and materials basis at a blended rate of {day_rate} per consultant day of eight hours, excluding VAT. Total fees under this Statement of Work may not exceed {fee_cap} without a signed change request, and the consultancy must warn Halvorsen in writing when eighty percent of the cap has been consumed. Timesheets are submitted weekly and approved within five working days. Travel to the main Halvorsen site is not chargeable; other travel is charged at cost under the Halvorsen expenses policy and needs prior approval. Invoices are issued monthly in arrears and paid on the payment terms of the master agreement.

The deliverables are listed in the annex, each with its acceptance criteria. When a deliverable is submitted, Halvorsen has {acceptance_days} to accept it or to list in writing how it fails the criteria. The consultancy then corrects the deliverable and resubmits it, and the review period starts again. If a deliverable fails acceptance twice, Halvorsen may require a third attempt at no charge, accept it with a fee reduction agreed in good faith, or terminate this Statement of Work and recover fees paid for that deliverable. A deliverable is deemed accepted if Halvorsen uses it in production or does not respond within the review period.

Either party may request a change in scope, timeline or staffing through the change request form. The consultancy assesses the impact on cost and timeline within five working days, and no work on the change starts until the form is signed. Changes with an estimated cost below {change_threshold} may be signed by the Halvorsen engagement manager alone; larger changes also need approval from the budget owner in finance. Delays caused by Halvorsen, such as late access or slow decisions, are recorded in the weekly status report and may justify a timeline change, but not additional fees unless the consultants were left idle for more than three working days.

title: Employment Contract Template: Permanent Employee
sections: This template is used for permanent, full time employees of {employer} whose normal place of work is {workplace}. It must not be edited outside the bracketed fields without approval from the legal team, and offers must be issued from the HR system so that the signed version is stored centrally. The hiring manager completes the job title, start date, salary and reporting line; all other terms below are fixed. Questions about the template go to the HR business partner, {person} ({email}). Fixed term contracts, apprentices and senior executives use separate templates, as do employees who will work mainly from another country.

Employment starts with a probationary period of {probation}, during which either party may end the contract on one week's notice, or the shorter notice the law allows. The manager holds a review meeting before the end of probation and confirms the outcome in writing; probation may be extended once where the law permits, if the employee has been absent or objectives are not yet met. Normal working time is {weekly_hours}, with flexible start and finish times around core hours of 10am to 4pm. Overtime is not paid for employees above the senior grade, but time off in lieu may be agreed with the manager in advance.

Salary is paid monthly in arrears by bank transfer on the last working day of the month and is reviewed annually in April, with no obligation to increase it. The company provides {pension}, subject to the scheme rules. Employees are entitled to {holiday} of paid holiday per year in addition to public holidays, accrued monthly; up to five unused days may be carried over to the first quarter of the next year. During sickness absence the employee receives {sick_pay}, provided the manager is notified before 10am on the first day of absence and medical certificates are supplied as required. Benefits such as health insurance are described in the benefits guide.

After probation, the employee must give {notice_employee} written notice to resign. The company must give the employee the same notice or the statutory minimum, whichever is longer. The company may place the employee on garden leave for all or part of the notice period, or pay salary in lieu of notice where the law allows. The company may end the contract without notice for gross misconduct following a fair disciplinary process. On termination the employee must return all company property, including laptops, access badges and documents, and accrued but untaken holiday is paid out or, where the law allows, deducted if taken in excess.

The employee must keep confidential all information about the company, its clients and its employees, both during and after employment. Intellectual property created in the course of employment belongs to the company. Outside work that may conflict with the employee's duties requires prior written approval. Personal data is processed as described in the employee privacy notice. This contract is governed by {governing_law}. Collective agreements apply only where stated in the contract or required by law. Signed contracts are countersigned by the people director, {person_2}, and a copy is provided to the employee within five working days of signature, together with the staff handbook.

title: Restrictive Covenants Policy: Non-Compete and Non-Solicitation
sections: This policy explains when Halvorsen Digital uses post-employment restrictive covenants for {covered_roles} employed under {jurisdiction}, and how they are drafted, paid for and enforced. Restrictions must be no wider than needed to protect client relationships, confidential information and the stability of the workforce; covenants that a court would see as excessive are unenforceable and damage our reputation as an employer. Covenants are included in contracts only through the approved clause bank, never drafted ad hoc by managers. Any request to add, tighten or remove a covenant for an individual employee is reviewed by employment counsel, {person} ({email}), before the offer or variation is issued.

The non-compete restriction prevents the employee, for {noncompete_months} after the end of employment, from working for or advising a competitor in a role similar to the one they held in their last twelve months with us. Competitors are businesses selling scheduling or workforce management software to the same customer segments, listed by name in an annex that is reviewed each year. The restriction applies only within {geography}. It does not stop the employee from holding up to three percent of the shares of a listed company, or from working for a customer of Halvorsen in an internal role that does not compete with our products.

Where a non-compete applies, the employee receives {nc_compensation} for every month of the restriction, paid monthly after employment ends where a payment is due. Payment stops if the employee breaches the covenant, and amounts paid during a breach may be reclaimed. The company may release the employee from the non-compete by written notice no later than {waiver_deadline}, in which case no compensation is due unless the law says otherwise. Any period of garden leave at the end of employment is {garden_leave_rule}. HR records every release decision in the leaver file so that payroll does not start or stop compensation payments by mistake.

For {nonsolicit_months} after employment ends, the employee may not solicit or deal with any client or prospective client with whom they had material dealings in their final twelve months, and may not solicit or hire any employee at manager grade or above with whom they worked closely. Responding to a general job advertisement is not solicitation. The non-solicitation covenant does not require compensation and applies whether or not the non-compete is released. Managers should remind leavers of these obligations in the exit interview, and the reminder is confirmed in the leaver letter, which lists the restrictions and their end dates.

If HR or a manager learns that a former employee may be breaching a covenant, they must not contact the individual or the new employer directly. The facts are passed to employment counsel, who decides within five working days whether to send a reminder letter, seek written undertakings or start proceedings. Proceedings require approval from the general counsel and the chief people officer, {person_2}. Evidence such as emails or public social media posts should be preserved, but never obtained by accessing personal accounts or devices. Covenants are reviewed every two years against current case law and legislation in each jurisdiction where we employ people.

title: Limitation of Liability and Indemnity Schedule
sections: This schedule sets out the agreed liability and indemnity position in the {agreement_type} between Halvorsen Digital and {counterparty} (the supplier). It was negotiated from the Halvorsen standard position and approved by the legal team; deviations recorded here prevail over the main terms. Neither party limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for any liability that cannot be limited by law. Commercial owners must check this schedule before agreeing to any change in scope that could increase exposure. The legal owner of this contract is {person} ({email}), who keeps the negotiation history and the approved fallback positions.

Subject to the unlimited liabilities above, each party's total liability arising out of or in connection with the agreement in any contract year, whether in contract, tort including negligence, or otherwise, is limited to {general_cap}. Where a claim relates to a single statement of work, the cap is calculated using the fees under that statement of work only if that produces a higher figure. Neither party is liable for loss of profits, revenue, goodwill or anticipated savings, or for any indirect or consequential loss, even if it was foreseeable. Service credits paid count towards the cap. Unpaid fees properly due are never subject to the cap.

Liability for breach of the data protection and confidentiality obligations is subject to a separate cap of {data_cap}, which applies in addition to, and not as part of, the general cap. This super-cap covers the reasonable costs of investigating a personal data breach, notifying regulators and data subjects, credit monitoring for affected individuals, and fines to the extent they can lawfully be recovered. Claims under the super-cap must be supported by evidence of the costs incurred. A breach caused by the supplier's failure to follow the security annex cannot be used to reduce its liability by arguing contributory fault on the part of Halvorsen.

The supplier will defend and indemnify Halvorsen against any third party claim that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights, and against the resulting damages, settlements and reasonable legal costs. Halvorsen must notify the supplier of the claim within {ip_notice} of becoming aware of it, give the supplier control of the defence, and provide reasonable assistance at the supplier's cost. The supplier may modify the deliverable to avoid infringement, procure a licence or, as a last resort, refund the fees paid for the affected item. The IP indemnity is uncapped. It does not apply to infringement caused by Halvorsen's modifications or by combination with products not supplied by the supplier.

The supplier maintains professional indemnity insurance of at least {pi_insurance} for each claim and in the aggregate, plus cyber insurance of an equivalent amount, for the term of the agreement and six years afterwards, and provides certificates each year on request. Any claim under the agreement must be notified in writing, with reasonable detail, within {claim_period} of the claimant becoming aware of the facts giving rise to it, and proceedings must start within twelve months after that notice. Claims notices go to the contract owner and to the supplier's legal contact, {person_2}. Each party must take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss.

title: Termination for Convenience and Exit Clause
sections: This clause note summarises the right of Halvorsen Digital to end the {agreement_type} with {counterparty} without cause, and the exit obligations that follow any termination. The right exists so that Halvorsen can respond to changes in strategy, budget or ownership without having to prove a breach. It is separate from termination for material breach, insolvency or chronic service failure, which are covered by their own clauses and carry no fee. Before any notice is sent, the business owner must obtain sign off from procurement and legal. The procurement lead for this contract is {person} ({email}), who also keeps the exit plan up to date.

Halvorsen may terminate the agreement, or any individual statement of work or service, for convenience by giving {notice_period} written notice. The right cannot be exercised so that termination takes effect before {lock_in}. Partial termination is allowed if the remaining services can operate on their own, and the fees are then reduced in proportion. The supplier has no right to terminate for convenience. Notice must be signed by an authorised signatory under the delegation of authority, and sent to the supplier's notice address and by email to its account director, {person_2}. A notice sent only by email is not effective under this agreement.

On termination for convenience Halvorsen pays all fees for services performed up to the termination date, plus {termination_fee}. Halvorsen also reimburses non-cancellable commitments that the supplier entered into specifically for Halvorsen with prior written approval, such as dedicated hardware or third party licences, after the supplier has used reasonable efforts to cancel or redeploy them. No payment is due for loss of profit on the cancelled services. The supplier must submit its final invoice with supporting evidence within thirty days after termination, and any amount not invoiced within that time is waived and cannot be claimed later.

From the date of notice the supplier must continue to perform the services to the contractual service levels until termination takes effect. On request, the supplier will provide exit assistance for up to {wind_down} after termination, including knowledge transfer sessions, handover of documentation and runbooks, and cooperation with any replacement supplier. Exit assistance beyond the activities in the agreed exit plan is charged at {transition_rate}. The exit plan is reviewed every year, and the supplier may not reduce the team assigned to Halvorsen during the notice period without consent, other than for reasons outside its control such as resignations.

Within {data_return} of termination, the supplier will return all Halvorsen data in an agreed open format, with a checksum report confirming completeness, and then delete all remaining copies and certify the deletion in writing. Until data is returned, the supplier may not suspend access to it, even if fees are disputed. Licences granted to Halvorsen for deliverables already paid for survive termination. Clauses on confidentiality, liability, intellectual property, data protection and payment of accrued fees also survive. Any dispute about exit charges is resolved through the escalation process, but it does not delay the return of data or the handover of services.

title: Renewal and Auto-Renewal Terms
sections: This summary covers the term and renewal provisions of the subscription with {vendor} for {product}. The agreement runs for an initial term of {initial_term} from the subscription start date shown on the order form. After that, it renews automatically for successive periods of {renewal_term} unless either party gives notice of non-renewal. Automatic renewal is convenient but has caused unplanned spend in the past, so every renewing contract has a named owner who must take an active decision before the notice deadline. The contract owner sits in {owner_team}, and the renewal record is maintained by {person} ({email}) in the contract register.

To stop the agreement renewing, notice of non-renewal must reach the vendor at least {nonrenewal_notice} before the end of the current term. Notice must be in writing and sent to the vendor's legal notice address with a copy to the account manager; cancelling through the vendor's online portal is only valid if the portal issues a written confirmation. Notice given late has no effect, and the agreement then renews for the full renewal period. The vendor is not required to remind Halvorsen of the deadline, although most vendors do. Notice of non-renewal may be withdrawn by mutual written agreement before the term ends.

On each renewal the fees may increase by up to {price_uplift}, provided the vendor gives written notice of the new fees at least ninety days before the end of the current term. If the vendor misses that deadline, the existing fees continue for the renewal period. Discounts granted for the initial term, such as launch or multi-year discounts, do not automatically carry over and must be renegotiated. Additional licences bought during a term are co-termed and renew at the same unit price as the main subscription. Halvorsen may reduce the licence count at renewal by up to twenty percent without penalty or loss of discount.

The contract register sends an automatic reminder to the contract owner {reminder_lead} before the non-renewal deadline, then again thirty days before it. On receiving the first reminder, the owner reviews usage, satisfaction and alternatives, and records a decision to renew, renegotiate or exit. Renewals above the owner's delegated authority require approval from the finance business partner before the deadline, not after the invoice arrives. If no decision is recorded fourteen days before the deadline, procurement escalates to the owner's director and may send a protective non-renewal notice to keep options open, which can later be withdrawn by agreement with the vendor.

Where Halvorsen exits at the end of a term, the vendor must make data available for export for thirty days and then delete it. Renewal does not reopen the liability, data protection or security terms unless either party requests a review in its renewal notice. Multi-year renewals require a business case reviewed by procurement. Questions about whether a renewal notice was validly given should be raised with the legal team immediately, with copies of all correspondence. The vendor's account manager for renewal discussions is {person_2}, but commercial negotiations are always led by procurement rather than by the business owner.

title: Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement
sections: This agreement is made between Halvorsen Digital and {contractor} (the Contractor) in connection with {project}. It records who owns the intellectual property in everything the Contractor creates for Halvorsen, including source code, designs, documentation, data models and inventions. It supplements the services agreement and prevails over it on any question of ownership. The Contractor confirms that every individual who works on the project, including employees and approved subcontractors, has signed terms that allow the Contractor to make this assignment. Halvorsen's contact for questions about ownership, licences and open source use is {person} ({email}) in the legal team.

The Contractor assigns to Halvorsen, with full title guarantee, all present and future intellectual property rights in the deliverables, by way of present assignment of future rights where the law allows. The assignment takes effect {assignment_trigger}. Until it takes effect, Halvorsen has an exclusive, royalty free licence to use the deliverables for the purposes of the project. The Contractor will sign any further documents needed to register or enforce the rights, at Halvorsen's cost, and appoints Halvorsen as its attorney to sign them if it fails to do so within ten working days of a written request from the legal team.

Background intellectual property means tools, libraries and know-how that the Contractor owned before the project or develops independently of it. Background IP stays with the Contractor. Where background IP is incorporated into a deliverable, the Contractor grants Halvorsen {background_licence}. The Contractor must list all background IP it intends to incorporate in the annex before using it, and anything not listed is treated as part of the deliverables and assigned with them. The Contractor may reuse general skills and know-how learned on the project, but never Halvorsen confidential information or code written for the deliverables, even in modified form.

{moral_rights} Open source software may be included in a deliverable only {open_source_rule}. Copyleft licences that would require Halvorsen to release its own source code are never permitted in deliverables distributed to customers. The Contractor provides a software bill of materials with every release, listing each third party component, its version and its licence. Halvorsen may run automated licence scanning on all code, and any component found that was not declared must be removed or replaced at the Contractor's cost within ten working days. Repeated undeclared components are treated as a material breach of the services agreement.

All source code, build scripts and documentation are committed to {delivery_repo} as the work progresses, and are never held only on the Contractor's own systems. On completion or termination, the Contractor deletes Halvorsen material from its systems, except one archival copy where required by law, and confirms deletion in writing. The Contractor warrants that the deliverables are its original work and do not infringe third party rights. This agreement is governed by {governing_law}. Notices to the Contractor are sent to its registered office and to its project lead, {person_2}, and take effect on receipt.

title: Limited Product Warranty
sections: Halvorsen Digital warrants that the {product} supplied to business customers in {region} will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use for {warranty_period} from the date of delivery. Batteries and other consumable parts are covered for {battery_period}. This warranty is given to the original purchaser only and is not transferable, except to a group company of the purchaser. It is in addition to any rights the customer has under mandatory law, which it does not limit. Proof of purchase, either the invoice or the delivery note showing the serial number, is required for any claim under this warranty.

To make a claim, the customer must report the defect through the support portal within {claim_window} of discovering it, giving the serial number, a description of the fault and the troubleshooting steps already taken. Support may ask for photos, logs or a remote diagnostic session before authorising a return. If a return is authorised, the customer receives a return merchandise authorisation number that must be shown on the outside of the package. {return_shipping} Devices returned without an authorisation number are sent back unrepaired at the customer's cost. The warranty desk can be reached on {phone} during business hours.

If a device is found to be defective and covered by the warranty, Halvorsen will, at its option, {remedy_order}. Replacement units may be new or refurbished to an equivalent standard of performance, and are covered for the remainder of the original warranty period or ninety days, whichever is longer. Data and configuration stored on the device are not covered, and the customer must back them up before returning it. Where a repair or replacement is not commercially reasonable, Halvorsen will refund the purchase price less a reasonable deduction for use. These remedies are the customer's sole remedies under this warranty.

The warranty does not cover damage caused by accident, misuse, liquid or dust ingress beyond the device's rated protection, power surges, unauthorised repair or modification, installation not in line with the installation guide, or use with accessories not approved by Halvorsen. Cosmetic wear that does not affect function, such as scratches on the housing, is also excluded. Software is covered by the separate subscription terms, not by this warranty. If a returned device is found to have no fault, or the fault is excluded, Halvorsen may charge a diagnostic fee of 60 euros or the local equivalent, plus return shipping.

Customers can extend cover by purchasing {extended_option} at the time of order or within ninety days of delivery. Extended cover includes advance replacement, in which a replacement device is shipped before the faulty device is returned, provided the faulty device is then returned within fifteen days. Extended cover cannot be added to devices that have already been reported as faulty. Warranty and extended cover questions from resellers go to the channel support manager, {person} ({email}). Halvorsen may update these terms for future orders, but changes never apply to devices that have already been delivered.
